meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Panama (Republic of Panama, unitary national jurisdiction, no sub-state tax distinction, Latin American dollarized financial and private-interest-foundation hub)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified 1917 Código Judicial and Código de Comercio; private corporate law anchored on Ley No. 32 de 1927; hybridized by common-law trust, private foundation, and general contract practice)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Bilateral Investment Treaty between the Republic of Panama and the United States of America (signed 27 April 1991; entered into force 12 October 1991)
Bilateral Investment Treaty between the Republic of Panama and the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland (signed 17 October 1985; entered into force 23 October 1993)
Bilateral Investment Treaty between the Republic of Panama and the Kingdom of the Netherlands (entered into force 2003)
Bilateral Investment Treaty between the Republic of Panama and the Federal Republic of Germany (signed 7 February 1985; entered into force 14 November 1988)
Convention between the Republic of Panama and the Republic of Italy for the Avoidance of Double Taxation with respect to Taxes on Income (signed 19 October 2009)
Free Trade Agreement between the Republic of Panama and the Republic of Chile (entered into force 2018)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley No. 21 de 29 de agosto de 2017 (AML/CFT legal framework for non-financial subjects, amending Ley 41 de 2007); Ley No. 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 (registration of beneficial owners, as amended by Ley No. 70 de 2019); Decreto Ejecutivo No. 363 de 29 de octubre de 2018 (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales maintained by the Dirección General de Ingresos); Acuerdo de Junta Directiva SIB No. 001-2020 (risk-based supervision of regulated entities); FATF Recommendation 24 and FATF post-plenary 2024 follow-up commitments.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national photo ID of each ultimate beneficial owner (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent passport, civil registry, or national identification authority of the owner's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961 Convention Contracting Parties) OR Consular Legalization at a Panamanian Embassy in non-Apostille countries

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation/Registration of any corporate UBO or intermediate holding entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registro Público de Panamá (for Panamanian entities) or the competent foreign commercial registry of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille in the jurisdiction of issuance; Consular Legalization if the origin state is not an Apostille Party

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney in favor of the Panamanian registered agent (Presidente/Representante Legal/Residente en Panamá)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Panamanian Notario Público (authenticating board resolutions and signing powers)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial authentication; additionally apostilled or consul-legalized if executed before a foreign notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter or 3-month certified source-of-funds statement linked to the escrow rail
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Originator bank of the shareholder or beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization for foreign-issued banking instruments; direct correspondent-bank verification acceptable under Panamanian due diligence standards

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Criminal record certificate of each director and UBO (antecedentes penales)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Procuraduría General de la Nación (Panama) or equivalent competent criminal-record authority abroad

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, intermediaries, and counterparties against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, UK/EU consolidated financial sanctions, and the Panamanian domestic PEP database (Ley 21/2017 Art. 7 and Decreto Ejecutivo 363/2018); enhanced due diligence (EDD) is compulsory for PEPs, high-risk jurisdictions, and cash-sensitive or escrow-intensive transactions; automated real-time screening with 5-year retention of risk files is required.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Portal de Servicios en Línea del Registro Público de Panamá (P.R. Digital) — https://www.registropublico.gob.pa
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed name must be submitted in Spanish or with a mandatory Spanish transliteration; the corporate suffix 'Sociedad Anónima' or 'S.A.' is compulsory; the name must be phonetically and grammatically distinct from any entity already registered; a minimum of three alternative names must be pre-submitted to permit immediate substitution upon rejection.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant files a written recurso de reconsideración before the Director General of the Registro Público within 5 business days, attaching the original name-search receipt (vista de nombre), the rejection notice, and revised alternative names; the Registry is statutorily required to respond within 10 business days. A further recurso de apelación may be lodged with the administrative appeals chamber of the Registro Público in accordance with Ley 38 de 2000; upon final confirmation of rejection, a fresh name-search application may be refiled immediately with a modified name without prejudice to the applicant.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office accepted for non-regulated holding and treasury functions of the S.A., but NOT acceptable as sole commercial substance for the ISIC 7810 study-abroad and immigration-consulting license: the Servicio Nacional de Migración and the Municipality of Panama require a verifiable physical office, a lease or sublease backed by a Panamanian responsible agent, and personnel present during business hours.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 45% quantified likelihood of unannounced on-site inspection during license application, renewal, or enhanced AML review; Municipality of Panama officials inspect Aviso de Operación compliance, and Servicio Nacional de Migración may perform random documentary and physical verification of in-country presence for licensed migration agents.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name search and reservation (vista de nombre) fee at the Registro Público
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff of the Registro Público fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Professional legal fee for drafting, review, and protocolization of the Articles of Incorporation of the Sociedad Anónima
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (450–1,200 USD typical range)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Incorporation registration fee (inscripción de la sociedad anónima) at the Public Registry
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff for corporate incorporation inscriptions

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and apostille/consular legalization bundle for UBO passports, powers of attorney, incumbency certificates, and police records
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notario Público and Registro Público (and Panamanian consular office where applicable)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff plus official apostille/consular processing fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Municipal business license (Aviso de Operación) application and registration
Beneficial Ownership Register (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales) initial filing and verification
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory annual administrative fee under Decreto Ejecutivo No. 363 de 2018

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Immigration services agent license and Servicio Nacional de Migración due diligence filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Servicio Nacional de Migración, Ministerio de Gobierno
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory administrative fee for regulated migration consultancy agents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Escrow account setup, KYB/KYC verification, and AML screening of counterparty payment rails (Escrow_Account and Wire_Transfer)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Panamanian or foreign licensed banking/escrow institution
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for corporate account opening and compliance due diligence

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley General de Sociedades (Law 32 of 1927), as amended by Law 5 of 2021, Articles 1-20, 29-39, 93-107; Código de Comercio de Panamá, Title I, Articles 360 et seq.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Entidades Jurídicas (Public Registry of Panama, Legal Entities Section)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución de Sociedad Anónima (Public Deed of Incorporation) including the Articles of Incorporation and Bylaws
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; authorized capital may be as low as US$10,000 and may be paid in installments. No escrow or notarized proof of payment is required by Ley 32 de 1927.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At a duly convened organizational meeting of the Board of Directors, the following resolutions were adopted: The subscription list is ratified and the authorized share capital is accepted, issued, and allotted to the initial subscribers. The registered office in Panama City is adopted, and the Secretary is directed to file the registered office notice and deliver all statutory books. The individuals named in this resolution are appointed as President, Secretary, and Treasurer, with full authority to open banking, escrow, and investment accounts, settle fiscal obligations, and execute contracts. All acts previously performed by the incorporator on behalf of the corporation are ratified in full.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Dirección de Entidades Jurídicas (online portal: www.registropublico.gob.pa)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application for certificate of availability (Certificado de Aprobación de Nombre) through the online 'Servicio de Búsqueda de Nombres' or in person at the Public Registry. Pay the official fee and indicate the proposed exact name; the system allows up to three alternative names. The certificate is valid for 90 days and must accompany the notarized incorporation deed.
required_dossiers: Application form with proposed corporate name (original and up to two alternatives)
Proof of payment of name search fee (approximately US$10)
Copy of incorporator's passport or DNI
Power of attorney if filed by a legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or already registered, file a short amendment to the application within 5 business days, offering another set of alternatives; no penalty is assessed if resubmitted within the 90-day reservation window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of the Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Panamanian Notary Public (Notaría Pública) in coordination with a licensed attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct counsel to draft the Escritura Pública de Constitución containing the company's name, purpose, capital structure, board provisions, and bylaws. The document must be executed before a notary by the incorporator(s) or attorney-in-fact. The notary will verify identity, witness signatures, and issue the authenticated deed ready for registration.
required_dossiers: Valid name reservation certificate from the Public Registry
Draft Articles of Incorporation and Bylaws
Identities and passports/DNI of all initial directors and officers
Notarized power of attorney if acting through an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects, the deed may be corrected and re-executed without additional registry fees, provided the name certificate remains valid. If the name expires, reserve a new name and re-execute.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Entidades Jurídicas (Mercantile Section)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized Escritura Pública with the Public Registry's Mercantile Section together with the corresponding registration form. Pay the registration fee (calculated based on authorized capital). Upon successful review, the Registry issues the Certificado de Inscripción (Certificate of Incorporation) confirming the company's legal existence and the official 'Personería Jurídica'.
required_dossiers: Notarized Escritura Pública de Constitución
Name reservation certificate
Proof of payment of registration fee
Two stamped copies of the Articles of Incorporation for the Registry's records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Public Registry issues a 'nota' (query or objection), legal counsel must respond within 15 business days by amending or clarifying the deed. A new certificate reservation is not required if the name is unchanged. Registry fees may be refunded or credited if the objections are procedural.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration (RUC) and Municipal Operating Notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Ministry of Economy and Finance; Municipalidad de Panamá (Office of Economic Merces)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply at the DGI's physical or online window for the Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC) using the corporate certificate and dissolution clause. After obtaining the RUC, file the Aviso de Operación (Operation Notice) with the Municipality of Panama City, submitting the required forms and sanitary and fire safety documents for review.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (Personería Jurídica)
RUC application form
Copy of Articles of Incorporation
Corporate letterhead and proof of registered office address
Fire safety inspection report from the Cuerpo de Bomberos
Municipal fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI or Municipal Office requests additional documentation, the applicant has 10 business days to re-present the dossier. Any delinquency fees may be waived within that period. In case of denials, file an appeal before the DGI's tax administrative chamber or the Mayor's office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Social Security and Labor Registry Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Caja de Seguro Social (CSS) – Registro de Empresa; Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as an employer with CSS within 15 days of hiring, completing form PE-1 and providing the RUC and corporate documents. Simultaneously, register the company and its occupational safety plan with MITRADEL's General Directorate of Occupational Health to obtain the workplace safety certificate required before operations.
required_dossiers: RUC certificate
Certificate of Incorporation
Power of attorney of the legal representative
Form PE-1 (employer registration)
Employees' identification documents
Framework and hygiene and safety plan
Rent or ownership deed of the office premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CSS or MITRADEL rejects the documents, correct the inconsistencies within 5 business days and resubmit. Appeals are allowed before the regional labor directorate. No operational license is withheld if the delay is procedural, but a provisional registration may be issued pending final compliance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Servicio Nacional de Migración (SNM) – Subdirección de Servicios Migratorios
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia de Agencia de Asesoría Migratoria y Estudiantil (Resolución de Operación Migratoria)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente de Panamá (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Evaluación y Control Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Categoría II – Aviso Ambiental / Registro de Bajo Impacto (office-based advisory, no physical transformation), requiring submission of a Ficha de Manejo Ambiental and obtaining an Certificado de Registro Ambiental.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Applies to office waste handling under Decree 71/2017: wastewater discharge to public systems must meet BOD5 ≤ 250 mg/L, TSS ≤ 250 mg/L, pH 6–8; VOCs from cleaning and AC systems must not exceed 12 mg/m³ (EPA Method 21) and all waste paper/aerosol cans must be segregated for municipal recycling. A minimum of 15% green area or compensatory planting is required for building occupancy permits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá verifying operational fire extinguishers, emergency egress, and smoke detectors; structural load inspection and uses-of-land permit from the Municipalidad de Panamá; occupational health and safety clearance from MITRADEL under Resolution 2017/001 for work-at-height and ergonomic risks in office environments.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas, República de Panamá; taxpayer portal: Sede Electrónica de la DGI at https://sede.dgi.gob.pa; electronic invoicing, RUC issuance, and tax filings are administered through this portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Panama Sociedad Anónima: (1) incorporate with the Registro Público de Panamá, file articles of incorporation, and appoint a resident agent (agente residente); (2) file the Aviso de Operación (Notice of Operation) electronically with the DGI through the Sede Electrónica, which constitutes the principal tax registration act and generates the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente); (3) obtain a DGI-accepted digital signature certificate (firma electrónica) for the legal representative; (4) obtain the municipal business license (Aviso de Operación Municipal) from the relevant Municipio; (5) register with the Caja de Seguro Social (CSS) and register as an employer upon hiring any Panama-based employees; (6) if the foreign entity performs no taxable activity in Panama and derives no Panama-source income, no RUC is required, and any Panama client's withholding agent files and remits taxes on a non-resident basis; a foreign entity merely invoicing Panama clients from abroad and performing all services abroad should not register as an ITBMS taxpayer.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not operate a U.S.-style check-the-box election nor a hybrid-mismatch entity election. Relevant statutory elections for a Panama S.A.: (i) small taxpayer regime (Régimen de Pequeño Contribuyente) under Law 135 of 2020, available where annual gross income does not exceed B/.150,000, substituting standard income tax and ITBMS obligations with a single 2% gross-receipts tax; (ii) Multinational Headquarters (SEM) license under Law 41 of 2007, as amended, for qualifying regional headquarters, granting defined income tax, ITBMS, and dividend exemptions; (iii) DGI authorization election for electronic invoicing models, either through the DGI's free web-based issuer or an accredited technology provider; (iv) election of the standard territorial-source taxation regime as reflected on the corporate income tax return (Form 201), under which only Panama-source income is subject to income tax and foreign-source income is excluded by statute. No consolidated tax filing, tax-transparent entity election, or hybrid-mismatch election is available for S.A. entities.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios), Panama's VAT-equivalent transfer tax on movable goods and services
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No fixed numeric threshold is codified as an ITBMS registration trigger; any natural or legal person habitually selling movable goods or rendering taxable services in Panama must register for ITBMS with the DGI. A separate simplified-regime ceiling of B/.150,000 (Panamanian balboas at 1:1 parity with USD) of annual gross income applies to the small taxpayer election, but this ceiling is not a general exemption from ITBMS registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama mandates a phased electronic invoicing (facturación electrónica) regime. Taxpayers must obtain an express habilitación (authorization) resolution from the DGI before issuing fiscal documents, either through the DGI's web-based issuer on the Sede Electrónica portal or through an accredited technology provider. Each electronic invoice, credit note, and debit note must be digitally signed, carry a DGI security code or validation stamp, and be transmitted to the DGI's fiscal repository within the approved transmission cycle; the DGI may impose real-time or near-real-time clearance requirements depending on the taxpayer's category and risk profile. Mandatory fields include the issuer's RUC, the customer's RUC (or passport for non-residents), the applicable ITBMS rate (7%, 0%, or exempt), and amounts expressed in balboas. Documents issued without the DGI security code or without timely transmission are treated as non-fiscal, exposing the issuer to fines and denial of input ITBMS credits; buyers may lawfully reject non-fiscal invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Panama's territorial ITBMS, a 0% zero-rated export treatment is available for qualifying exports of goods and exports of services. For goods: the taxpayer must be a registered Panamanian seller, the goods must physically depart Panama, and the export must be validated through the unified customs declaration. For services: the service must be rendered by a Panamanian supplier to a non-resident recipient, performed and benefited wholly outside Panama, with no local consumption within Panama, and the supplier must retain the service contract, an export invoice, and evidence that payment was routed from abroad. For the analyzed scope (international student placement and immigration/golden visa advisory), Panamanian visa applications and residency filings are consummated in Panama and the benefit is enjoyed in Panama, so the standard 7% ITBMS applies to local immigration work; only clearly offshore placement services, where the beneficiary is domiciled abroad, no Panamanian admissions step is performed, and the benefit is realized wholly abroad, may be documented as zero-rated exports. Input ITBMS attributable to genuine exports is creditable or refundable through the monthly ITBMS return. Panama imposes no statutory FX repatriation deadline; the 180-day benchmark stated below is the customary documentary window applied by Panamanian banks and the DGI for export proceeds realization and zero-rating substantiation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única de Exportación / DUA) stamped and verified by the Servicio Nacional de Aduanas
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure of the goods from Panama
Commercial invoice and packing list in Spanish as required by customs regulations
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 credit evidence from a Panama-regulated bank showing payment received from the foreign buyer
Export service contract and certificate of use and benefit abroad for zero-rated service exports
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI and the Servicio Nacional de Aduanas jointly enforce export zero-rating. A false export declaration, forged customs or transport documentation, or a sham offshore-services structure (e.g., services actually consumed in Panama, artificial pass-through of local services, or circular invoicing with related parties) triggers: immediate revocation of the zero-rating; retroactive assessment of the omitted 7% ITBMS plus statutory interest from the date the tax was due; monetary fines and surcharges under the Panamanian Tax Code, calculated on the tax omitted; denial of input ITBMS credits associated with the fraudulent transactions; and criminal referral for the offense of defraudación tributaria (tax fraud), which is punishable by imprisonment under Panamanian law. Retrospective clawback reaches the open statutory limitation periods, and where the fraud was directed or approved by the S.A.'s directors, officers, or legal representative, such persons may be held jointly and severally liable for the assessed tax, interest, and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) as the banking and AML/CFT supervisor; Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as fiscal agent and clearing agent. Panama has no currency-issuing central bank; the US dollar is legal tender.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama is a fully dollarized economy with no foreign exchange controls and full convertibility on both current and capital account transactions. Profit remittance and dividend distribution are unrestricted from an exchange-control perspective, but payment channels are subject to bank-level KYC, AML/CFT reviews, and FATF-aligned due diligence. Practical hurdles arise only from documentary verification, beneficial ownership disclosure, and source-of-funds substantiation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender requirements or mandatory conversion ratios apply to export proceeds. Exporters may freely retain, disburse, or reinvest US-dollar receipts. The only obligations are accounting, tax, and AML/CFT record-keeping duties, including traceability of cross-border wire flows and suspicious transaction reporting.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-medium feasibility. Panama does not have a dedicated EU-style electronic money institution (EMI) licensing regime. Offshore digital EMIs are generally not permitted to provide payment accounts to Panamanian corporate entities without a locally licensed fintech or banking partner. Any cross-border EMI arrangement must rely on a licensed Panamanian bank for clearing and settlement; otherwise the unlicensed collection of client funds may constitute a banking or AML violation under the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá framework.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Panamanian banks generally require directors, shareholders, and authorized signatories to attend an in-person KYC interview at a branch or before a notarized corporate authorization is accepted. Remote opening is possible only for already-existing clients or through regulated virtual banking arrangements, but for a newly incorporated Sociedad Anónima in the immigration-visa advisory sector a physical appearance of the legal representative and compliance officer is the prevailing commercial and regulatory expectation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity due to Panama S.A. share structure and non-resident shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate registry excerpt showing legal entity details; sworn declaration of ultimate beneficial owner; passport copies and tax identification numbers of all shareholders; notarized corporate resolutions; legal opinion from a Panamanian attorney confirming ownership chain and absence of bearer-share control issues.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk business profile involving study abroad and immigration visa fee collection
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sectoral license issued by the Panamanian immigration or tourism authority; detailed business plan and client onboarding policy; anti-money laundering (AML) manual; risk assessment; contractual templates for student counseling and visa advisory services; segregation of client funds and escrow account agreements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors or politically exposed persons in the ownership chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP declaration forms for all directors and beneficial owners; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation; independent lawyer certification; enhanced due diligence questionnaire; corporate group structure chart and jurisdictional explanation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual funding patterns or cross-border capital injections without clear commercial nexus
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed service agreements and invoices; escrow client ledger; proof of underlying contracts with foreign educational institutions or immigration authorities; bank reference letters; audit trail of funds by wire confirmation and SWIFT purpose codes.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections should be routed through SWIFT MT103 wire transfers to a Panamanian bank account using the corporate legal name and standardized narrative 'Capital Contribution for Corporate Treasury Purposes – Non-Refundable'. The sending institution must include the full corporate registration number, registered address, and ultimate beneficial owner information. Verification is performed by the receiving bank against the entity registry and KYC file. Where required, a notarized corporate resolution and board authorization confirming the capital injection must be attached. Panama’s dollarized system clears USD funds through correspondent banks in the United States via Fedwire or CHIPS; therefore, all narrations must avoid restricted trade or migration terms that could be misclassified as third-party client money.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements are executed primarily by SWIFT MT103 or SWIFT MT202 for bank-to-bank settlements, with commercial letters of credit and documentary collections used where the underlying immigration or study abroad service involves milestone-based payments to foreign universities, visa authorities, or accommodation providers. Escrow accounts in Panama provide a compliant clearing rail for holding client funds pending performance milestones. Disbursements must be supported by service contracts, invoices, and visa application confirmations. All transactions must pass through the corporate operational account and must be reconciled with the territorial income tax net; banks will require CF/Invoice and contract details for higher-value outward transfers.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Cross-currency forward contracts (USD against Euro, GBP, and other major student-outbound currencies)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) with approved counterparties where local settlement is constrained
Currency swaps between USD and foreign education-market currencies
Vanilla foreign exchange options with licensed Panamanian banks or international counterparties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax (Impuesto Anual sobre Personas Jurídicas)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due March 15 each year; optional installment payments due by March 15, June 15, and September 15
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late payment surcharge plus monthly interest of 1.5%; continued non-payment leads to registration suspension and administrative strike-off after extended delinquency

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 for calendar-year taxpayers (fiscal year ended December 31)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to USD 1,000 for late filing; monthly interest on any tax due; criminal penalties for willful concealment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner Registry Declaration (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Superintendencia de Sujetos No Financieros (SSNF), formerly UAF
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by March 31; immediate update within 30 days of any shareholding or control change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of USD 50 to USD 5,000 depending on entity size; repeat non-filing can trigger corporate suspension and restriction of bank account operations

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit required when annual gross income exceeds USD 1,500,000, when total assets exceed USD 3,000,000, or when holding client escrow funds under immigration-consulting license conditions; statutory audit also required for public-interest and regulated financial activities
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as adopted by Panama; IFRS for SMEs permitted for private entities below the audit threshold

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every S.A. must file an annual declaration confirming current ultimate beneficial owners with the SSNF. Any transfer of shares or changes in control must be reported within 30 days, and the annual registry declaration must identify all natural persons holding >10% equity or who ultimately direct the entity, including for golden visa and study-abroad escrow arrangements.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 - USD 5,000 when audit triggers exceeded

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial taxation: income sourced abroad is outside the Panamanian tax base for a Sociedad Anónima. No general tax holiday exists for standard advisory companies, but preferential regimes may apply to qualifying entities such as Multinational Headquarters (SEM) licensees taxed at 5% of qualifying income, and licensed free-zone or Ciudad del Saber operators that can access full exemptions. A study-abroad and visa advisory S.A. may structure cross-border service delivery so that fees for services rendered and consumed entirely outside Panama are treated as non-taxable foreign-source income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 02 (Declaración Jurada de Renta) filed electronically through the DGI's SIVE online filing portal; authorized public accountants may file on behalf of the S.A.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three calendar months after the fiscal year-end. For a calendar-year S.A., the statutory deadline is 31 March of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All gross revenue recognized from Panamanian-source activities, including advisory fees, placement commissions, and visa-processing charges earned through services performed or consummated in Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident-owned S.A. must include only Panamanian-source income. Fees from student placement or visa advisory work completed outside Panama are excluded and should be supported by contracts, dated service reports, and evidence of the location of personnel and delivery.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income claimed as territorial exemption or treaty-relieved income, including foreign advisory income, foreign dividends, and interest from non-Panamanian sources.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a schedule detailing each foreign-source revenue stream, counterparty jurisdiction, and documentary proof of foreign economic activity. DTA-reduced income must be tied to a valid tax residence certificate from the treaty partner.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ordinary and necessary expenses directly or indirectly allocable to the production of Panamanian-source taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apportion expenses between taxable Panamanian-source activity and non-taxable foreign-source activity. Expenses incurred solely for foreign operations are not deductible against Panamanian taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Panama-source gross income minus allowable deductions, adjusted for any transfer-pricing corrections.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-controlled S.A. must confirm that cross-border payments to related parties have not been denied or adjusted under the arm's-length principle before entering this net figure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax computed by applying the 25% flat statutory corporate income tax rate to net taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: There are no graduated brackets. A nil amount is acceptable only if the S.A. demonstrates the absence of Panama-source income or zero net taxable income after correct deduction treatment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Prepayments, Withholdings, and Tax Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance income tax payments, payroll withholding credits, foreign tax credits available under domestic law, and any DTA credits previously approved by the DGI.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only credits legally documented and traceable through the SIVE system should be entered. Tax withheld at source on Panamanian-interest or dividend income must be supported by annual withholding certificates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Resulting tax liability after applying Box 6 credits, or refundable excess if prepayments and withholdings exceed total liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any balance due must be paid through authorized Panama banking wire transfer before filing acceptance is completed. Refund requests involving territorial exclusions require additional legal narrative and documentation in SIVE.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a monthly surcharge of 5% of the tax due for each month or fraction of a month of delay, capped at 50% of the tax due, plus monetary interest at 1.5% per month. Administrative non-compliance can lead to suspension of the RUC (taxpayer ID), blocked access to public contracts, and forced-estimate assessments by the DGI.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends distributed by a non-listed Panama S.A.; 5% on dividends from shares listed on the Panama Stock Exchange or recognized public securities markets. Dividends paid out of income already taxed at the full corporate rate remain subject to the shareholder-level withholding, unless reduced under an applicable income tax treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident shareholder must obtain a valid tax residence certificate (TRC) from the competent authority of the treaty jurisdiction, submit the DGI-prescribed relief application before the dividend distribution date, and provide any requested beneficial-ownership declaration. The DGI will issue a specific approval or certificate of lower withholding; until that approval is obtained, the S.A. must withhold at the statutory 10% rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding: 12.5% on royalties for the use or right to use IP, trademarks, models, plans, or specialized know-how exploited in Panama; 6% on interest paid to non-resident lenders where the underlying debt is effectively connected to Panamanian activities. Treaty-reduced rates apply only after TRC and DGI approval. Technical service fees for services physically rendered outside Panama are generally not Panama-source and are not subject to withholding.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Master File are triggered when annual gross revenue in the preceding fiscal year exceeds B/.3,000,000 (Panamanian Balboa, pegged 1:1 to the U.S. dollar), or whenever the S.A. has cross-border transactions with related parties exceeding B/.1,000,000 and applies a preferential tax regime. Country-by-Country Reporting filing applies where a multinational group meets the OECD consolidated revenue threshold as domesticated under Panamanian law.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP (Comparable Uncontrolled Price) for placement commissions and student recruitment fees
Resale Price Method for sub-agent and intermediary arrangements
Cost Plus Method for routine study-counseling and visa-processing services
TNMM (Transactional Net Margin Method) as the default method for cross-border immigration advisory services
Profit Split Method for integrated multi-jurisdiction arrangements involving significant intangibles and entrepreneurial risk
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Economic Substance Regulations apply to entities carrying on relevant activities, which include professional services such as advisory, consultancy, and immigration-visa services. The S.A. must maintain a real physical office in Panama, employ qualified staff working in Panama, incur minimum local operating expenditure proportional to income, and hold board meetings and strategic decisions in Panama. Failure to satisfy substance requirements will cause the tax authority to disregard claimed territorial treatment, reclassify revenue as Panamanian-source, and deny treaty or incentive benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion — False or Omitted Panama-Source Income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Mischaracterizing visa-advisory and student-placement income as foreign-source when staff perform services in Panama, contracts are executed in Panama, or the commercial activities are effectively controlled from Panama; also filing Form 02 with a zero tax base while maintaining substantial bank deposits in Panama.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Omitted tax is immediately assessable plus monthly interest and an additional surcharge of up to 100% of the omitted amount. Criminal tax fraud prosecutions carry fines and imprisonment under the Panamanian Fiscal Code; the S.A.'s RUC may be suspended and its commercial registry operations blocked.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who sign false or fraudulent tax declarations become personally liable for restitution where the corporation is used as a mere instrumentality. Courts may pierce the corporate veil and impose travel bans, asset seizures, professional disqualification, and imprisonment for fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The S.A. is registered at an off-the-shelf law-firm address, has no physical Panama office and no locally employed administrators, yet relies on territorial treatment or free-zone incentives to strip taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of territorial exemptions, re-characterization of all income as Panama-source taxable at 25%, penalties of up to 50% of the corrected tax liability, and possible administrative cancellation of the corporate license by the Superintendency of Non-Financial Entities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Registered agents and directors may be sanctioned for facilitating an economic-substance sham; they face monetary fines, suspension of professional practice, and personal responsibility for tax arrears if they knowingly participated in misrepresentation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare and submit Local File, Master File, or annual transfer pricing return when related-party transactions exceed Panama's thresholds, or using non-arm's-length margins for management fees charged to the study-abroad or visa-consulting structure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Mandatory TP adjustment to arm's-length result, plus interest and penalty of 10% to 30% of the adjustment; administrative fines for non-filing of documentation can reach B/.50,000, and the DGI may terminate audit proceedings in favor of the taxpayer only after full compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who execute related-party contracts at artificial prices may be jointly and severally liable for the resulting TP adjustment and penalties, particularly where distribution to foreign owners is disguised as deductible fees to strip Panama earnings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML — Escrow and Tuition-Fund Handling Violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating student-placement and golden-visa escrow accounts without customer due diligence, beneficial ownership records, or suspicious-transaction reporting; using client tuition or immigration investment funds to purchase Panamanian bearer assets, or accepting funds known to originate from migrant-smuggling, fraud, or corruption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Panama's Law 23 of 2015 and AML regulations, fines range from thousands to millions of balboas depending on severity and the value of unlawful transactions, with additional confiscation of criminal proceeds. Repeat violations cause forced administrative dissolution, prohibition from the regulated immigration-advisory sector, and criminal prosecution for money laundering with imprisonment up to 10 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors responsible for AML compliance may face incarceration, personal fines, travel bans, and extradition cooperation in cross-border cases. Panama courts will pierce the S.A. when the corporate form is used as a laundering conduit, making shareholders and beneficial owners directly liable, not merely the entity.
